title: Janapada of Kuru
capsule: The Kuru kingdom was a Vedic Indo-Aryan polity in the upper Gangetic-Yamuna plain, formed through the amalgamation of the Bharata and Puru tribes around 1200–1100 BCE and constituting what is considered the first documented state-level society in the Indian subcontinent. Its political and religious centre was Āsandīvat (early capital), later supplemented by Hastinapura and Indraprastha (near modern Delhi), and Kuru scholars standardized Vedic ritual texts and early Upanishadic thought. The kingdom suffered a decisive defeat by the Salva tribe and was significantly diminished by the eighth century BCE, surviving only as a minor janapada until absorption into the Nanda Empire around 345 BCE. The Mahabharata epic preserves a legendary account of Kuru dynastic conflict centred on the kings Parikshit and Janamejaya.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Vedic textual sources provide good attestation for the kingdom's existence and cultural achievements, but territorial boundaries are reconstructed from literary and archaeological evidence (Painted Grey Ware sites) and remain approximate.
